Brendan McDermid | Reuters U.S. equity futures jumped early Thursday as investors looked ahead to Anthropic's public trading debut. Futures tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.38%. S&P 500 futures added 0.59%, and Nasdaq-100 futures surged 0.99% In Asia, markets were mostly lower. South Korea's Kospi fell 0.25% as markets opened an hour later than usual due to the country's annual college entrance exam . Hong Kong's Hang Seng index fell 1.89%, while mainland China's CSI 300 declined 0.49%. Australia's S&P/ASX 200 closed 1.08% lower. Japan's Nikkei 225 rose 0.48%, while the Topix fell 0.15%. In Wednesday's regular U.S. trading, the blue-chip Dow lost more than 560 points, or 1.1%. The broad market S&P 500 fell 0.2%, marking its fifth consecutive losing session and longest slide since June. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite rose 0.4%. Traders are focused on how the company behind Claude performs when it debuts on the Nasdaq Thursday, trading under the ticker "ANT." The artificial intelligence company priced its initial public offering at $83 a share, above the expected range, a person familiar with the matter told CNBC Wednesday. Anthropic also upsized the offering, selling around 980 million shares, bringing the amount raised to $81.3 billion and surpassing SpaceX, which held a record IPO in June. The market has become more cautious on AI as of late, with investors focusing on whether heavy spending on the build-out will translate into meaningful profits. The iShares AI Innovation and Tech Active ETF (BAI) has fallen 11% this month, and embattled AI bellwether Nvidia has dropped 26% while the company grapples with the resignation of its CEO Jensen Huang. Shares of neocloud CoreWeave , which had seen its bond yields trade above 16% earlier this month, is also down almost 13% in November alone. "It'll be an important barometer for investors' AI appetite," Callie Cox, director of investment strategy at Plancorp, said of Anthropic's IPO. "AI stocks desperately need some wind at their backs, too ... Wall Street needs a sign that investors still believe in the potential for AI beyond already-elevated expectations." "The challenge in that thesis is that hot IPOs rarely perform well right out of the gate, especially these days, when every company seems to be vying for a limited pool of capital to fund their AI strategy," she said. "While I wouldn't be surprised to see the stock market take cues from Anthropic's performance, I'd caution investors about trying to read the tea leaves from one event too much." On Thursday, traders will keep an eye out for weekly jobless claims. Travis Dove | Bloomberg | Getty Images Walmart is scheduled to report its third fiscal quarter earnings Thursday as the retailer prepares for the holiday season with an increased emphasis on value amid lower consumer sentiment. The big-box retailer has posted solid growth over the past few quarters as it sees customers gravitate to reduced prices, improvements in delivery and gains in its advertising business. It's also leaned into attracting higher-income consumers with its Walmart+ membership. Here's what the company is expected to report for its fiscal third quarter, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG: Earnings per share: 64 cents expected Revenue: $187.27 billion expected Walmart previously said it expects third-quarter net sales to climb 3% to 3.75%. CFO John David Rainey told CNBC last quarter that Walmart's "business is strong" and that he's encouraged by its progress. The company is typically well insulated from macroeconomic pressures because of its value reputation. Last quarter, the company said it was lowering prices of products across multiple categories, including beef. It also saw a significant boost from tariff refunds, which Rainey said Walmart would use to cut prices. In October, Walmart announced it was launching a joint membership option with its club subsidiary, Sam's Club, as it leans further into convenience. Both stores will still offer standalone memberships. The retailer is also rolling out technology in its stores to improve the customer experience, including light-up digital shelf labels that are connected to its app. Those shelf labels and Walmart's AI push have also sparked concerns that the retailer could try to change prices based on demand and shoppers' personal data, which Walmart has denied. Analysts from UBS wrote in a note last week that they believe the retailer's fiscal third-quarter results will show healthy market share gains. "E-commerce continues to scale, the company's higher-margin alternative revenue streams continue to grow and Walmart is increasingly able to fund investments in price and convenience while still producing attractive operating income growth," the analysts wrote. They added that they expect Walmart's fourth-quarter outlook to include "robust operating income growth." Shares of Walmart have fluctuated this year but are up roughly 13% year-to-date. headlines.article_text: Musk says Jensen Huang is irreplaceable, regrets midterm spending Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Elon Musk said at the NYT DealBook Summit that ousting Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO did not seem like a "smart decision." Musk added he felt "pretty foolish" about spending at least $474 million on the U.S. midterms. On a possible SpaceX-Tesla merger, Musk said areas of overlap between the companies now exist that "didn't exist before." In this article NVDA Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT (L-R) Andrew Ross Sorkin and Elon Musk speak during the NY Times Dealbook Summit at Jazz at Lincoln Center, Nov. 18, 2026 in New York City. Adam Gray | Getty Images Elon Musk compared Jensen Huang 's departure from Nvidia to kicking Michael Jordan off a team on a winning streak, while also expressing regret over how much he spent on the U.S. midterms. "You've got a winning streak ... and then you kick Michael Jordan off your team," Musk told Andrew Ross Sorkin at The New York Times' DealBook Summit on Wednesday. He added, "Doesn't seem like a smart decision to me." watch now VIDEO 1:25 01:25 Elon Musk: Everyone I know thinks Jensen Huang should have stayed on as Nvidia CEO News Videos Huang resigned last week following pressure after disclosing an affair with a woman who reportedly was suspected of being a Chinese spy, alongside reports of relationships with employees. He is expected to testify before the U.S. Congress next month around national-security and export-control issues. The SpaceX and Tesla chief executive, who previously said it would be an "honor" to hire the Nvidia co-founder, added that no one could really replace Huang. Musk said he had heard similar views about Huang's departure from Nvidia, including from President Donald Trump . "I think the president has voiced publicly that he thinks Jensen should have stayed as CEO, and everyone I know thinks the same ... this is, at the end of the day, the Nvidia board decision," he said, adding, "We're not on the board, right?" Musk and Huang have known each other for years through Nvidia's work with Tesla and OpenAI. Tesla has been a major Nvidia customer, while Huang has repeatedly praised Musk's AI strategy, including Tesla's self-driving work, xAI and the Optimus robot. Midterms, Tesla and SpaceX Asked about the midterms, Musk said he felt "pretty foolish" about spending at least $474 million with little to show for it, though he added that "maybe it would have been much worse without that." Musk said his goal had been to prevent the presidency, House and Senate from all being controlled by one party. "If I could rewind the clock, I would have spent less money," he said. watch now VIDEO 2:43 02:43 Elon Musk: If I could rewind the clock, I would have spent less money on U.S. midterms News Videos In the same interview, he also appeared to distance himself from the MAGA movement. "I'm not MAGA," he said, adding that he wasn't sure what the term means. On a possible SpaceX-Tesla merger, Musk said areas of overlap now exist that "didn't exist before," pointing to AI, robotics and the AI software and chip-design teams at both companies. He said any deal would require shareholder approval and "may or may not succeed." Musk added that he could not push through a transaction that was bad for shareholders because he would "obviously get sued." Asked whether he should receive his Tesla pay award if a merger were completed, Musk said he should not be rewarded "just for doing a merger" and should receive stock-option awards only if Tesla meets its performance targets. Musk also said SpaceX rents computing capacity to Anthropic under short-term agreements that either side can terminate, adding that the Claude AI chatbot-maker had expressed interest in an additional 10 gigawatts. watch now VIDEO 2:28 02:28 Elon Musk: More areas of overlap between SpaceX and Tesla than before News Videos Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share on Wednesday, raising $81.3 billion in what it said was the largest public offering on record, surpassing SpaceX. Asked how he feels a year after describing his mind as "a storm," Musk said he feels "relatively at peace." headlines.article_text: Anthropic IPO raises over $81 billion in largest offering on record Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share, above the expected range. The AI company is expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol "ANT" on Thursday. Anthropic upsized its offering and sold about 980 million shares, raising $81.3 billion. In this article ANT Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Anthropic co-founder and CEO Dario Amodei speaks during INBOUND 2025 Powered by HubSpot at Moscone Center in San Francisco, Sept. 4, 2025. Chance Yeh | Getty Images Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share on Wednesday, above the expected range, setting the stage for the Claude creator's eagerly awaited Nasdaq listing and a historic moment for the artificial intelligence industry. The company, along with its seven co-founders, upsized the offering, selling about 980 million shares, according to a press release . That brings the amount raised to $81.3 billion, surpassing SpaceX, which held a record IPO in June. Elon Musk's company raised $75 billion initially and a total of $85.7 billion after underwriters exercised their overallotment. Anthropic's fully diluted market cap sits at around $1.5 trillion. The stock is expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker symbol "ANT." The listing is a major test for the AI industry, which has experienced a set of recent shocks, including a dramatic backlash that was felt at the polls in the midterm elections and last week's ouster of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang . The market was already jittery on concerns that rising interest rates will make debt unaffordable for many data center developers and neoclouds. After publicly unveiling its prospectus in October, Anthropic updated the document last week with an expected price range between $70 and $78 per share. The company had been planning to sell 825 million shares. Tech's biggest companies have significant exposure to Anthropic, as an investor, partner or customer. Amazon and Google both own stakes valued at over $100 billion, and a group of tech companies, including Google, Microsoft , Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices agreed to collectively invest $26 billion at the IPO price. Anthropic, meanwhile, is a buyer of costly systems from Nvidia, Google, Amazon and AMD. "We have to make sure that all the risks, all the ways that things can go wrong with this technology, we very carefully address those risks as we bring the benefits and as we have a viable business at the same time." Amodei co-founded Anthropic in 2021 alongside a handful of other researchers less than six years ago, after the group collectively defected from OpenAI. The company is best known for developing a family of AI models called Claude , and it primarily sells its products and services to other businesses. According to the latest prospectus, each co-founder is selling 3.38 million shares for total proceeds of $1.96 billion. Anthropic has been racing to maintain an edge over OpenAI and Google in the enterprise market, and it experienced a period of explosive growth in 2026, driven largely by the popularity of its AI coding tool, Claude Code. OpenAI has confidentially filed for an IPO and has said a debut is likely in 2027. For the nine months ended Sept. 30, Anthropic said, it generated $33.24 billion in revenue, up roughly 1,200% from the same period last year, according to its prospectus. The company reported a $104 billion net loss during the nine-month period, though most of that was due to the change in fair value of convertible notes and derivative liabilities. Anthropic lost $25.1 billion over the same stretch in 2025, the filing said. Anthropic said in an amended filing that its run-rate revenue was roughly $81 billion at the end of October, up $10 billion from the previous month. The company has faced plenty of challenges during its meteoric rise over its positions on safety, regulation and national security, leading to two high-profile disputes with the U.S. government this year. Its prospectus included more than 90 pages of risk factors for investors to consider ahead of its IPO. "Our aim is to help humankind chart a safe course through this technological evolution, open new frontiers of discovery, and bring forth an age of miracles," Anthropic's co-founders wrote in the company's prospectus. "Everyone who owns our stock, whether an institution or an individual, becomes part of that effort."
